The image shows a leaf with:
- Multiple irregular, pale grayish-white powdery patches scattered across the upper leaf surface
- Patches are somewhat circular to irregular in shape
- The underlying leaf tissue beneath patches appears slightly discolored/chlorotic
- No dark necrotic lesions with defined margins (rules out Anthracnose)
- No sooty black coating (rules out Sooty Mould)
- No dieback/shoot tip death (rules out Die Back)
- The white-gray powdery residue on the leaf surface is classic for a fungal surface colonization

This pattern — discrete powdery white/gray colonies on the leaf surface — is characteristic of **Powdery Mildew** (*Oidium mangiferae* on mango). The fungal mycelium and conidia form the white mealy patches directly on the leaf epidermis.
